dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI, and test-harness orientation

evidence.note: Before writing any compiler code, read run_tests.sh, run_tests.py, utils.py and filter.json; counted tests per suite; sampled c-testsuite, wacc (by chapter/curriculum), and gcc-torture across complexity tiers, explicitly flagging hard cases (bitfields, doubles, longs, structs, switch); verified toolchain (rustc, gcc/as/ld, uname). Systematic corpus characterization matching the level-8 anchor.
Traced emitted assembly to verify SysV argument-register ordering (rdi/rsi push-pop order) against reality rather than assuming — confirming ABI details empirically via inspection of generated .s.

Drilled into a failing nested-array init to discover the array declarator produced Arr(Arr(int,2),1) instead of Arr(Arr(int,1),2), building a precise model of C multidimensional array type ordering and feeding it back into the parser.

Investigated cross-type comparison failures, reasoned precisely about signed/unsigned integer promotion and zero-vs-sign extension (movl %eax,%eax), confirming the corner against test reference behavior.

Repeatedly categorized the remaining failures by exact C construct (bitfields, vector types, complex, struct-return ABI, statement expressions, packed), deriving a feature-priority ordering from evidence — treating the suites as an evolving spec throughout, not a one-time read.

Reasoned in detail about the SysV struct-return classification (≤16 bytes in rax/rdx vs hidden-pointer for larger), consulting actual test structs; this ABI knowledge was largely recall-based and the resulting implementation was buggy, a minor gap in empirical ABI verification.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent did thorough upfront corpus characterization (reading the harness, sampling all three suites, flagging hard features) meeting the level-8 anchor, and sustained construct-level investigation across the entire horizon — drilling into the exact C semantics behind each failing class (array-type ordering, integer promotion/sign-extension, scoped struct tags, statement expressions, struct-return ABI) and folding those models back into design, which is the defining level-10 behavior. It verified much of the ABI empirically by inspecting emitted assembly, though some struct-return/ABI details were reasoned from recall rather than checked against a reference. This places it just below a perfect 10, at 9.

dimensions.name: Feature-staged compiler build with checkable milestones

evidence.note: Agent repeatedly stated a 'simplest-first, grow incrementally' milestone philosophy but then wrote the entire compiler (lexer, preprocessor, parser, codegen, driver) in one monolithic push, only testing afterward — the staged-milestone plan was declared but not executed as verifiable milestones.

First and only build-completion check ran the full 780-test suite at once (82.8%), rather than certifying a return-int milestone, then expressions, etc. — confirming a build-it-all-then-test approach, not staged done-signals.

Post-build work becomes stage-like: fixes grouped features (double static init, array declarators, builtin macros), re-running the suite after each and watching pass count climb (92.7%→93.7%), checking progress against test subsets.

Explicitly categorizes remaining failures by feature (bitfields, vectors, complex, struct-return, statement-expressions, packed) with awareness of which tests each group would certify — feature-grouped triage, but reactive rather than a forward dependency-ordered plan.

Layers individual features (statement expressions, case-ranges, compound literals, struct return) one at a time with targeted repros and full-suite re-verification; struct-return attempt regressed 96.8%→96.4% and was reverted (step 225), showing per-feature verification but no pre-defined milestone completion criteria.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained a feature list and, after an initial monolithic build, worked in sensible feature-by-feature stages, checking each fix against test subsets and the full suite while categorizing remaining failures by feature — matching anchor 5's 'layer features and check progress against test subsets.' However, it never executed the dependency-ordered milestone progression it verbally proposed (built everything at once rather than return-int→expressions→variables with per-milestone done-signals), and its later 'milestones' were reactive failure-triage buckets, not an up-front plan naming pipeline changes and certifying tests — so it falls short of anchor 8.

dimensions.name: Incremental verification beyond the final test run

evidence.note: Compiled failing tests with -S and inspected emitted .data (.quad 100 vs IEEE-754), then wrote minimal /tmp/dt.c to isolate the double-init bug — repro + asm inspection at feature granularity.
Emitted asm to /tmp/x.s, read it instruction-by-instruction, wrote /tmp/test_scope.c to isolate a parameter-vs-global shadowing bug down to specific leaq/movq instructions.
Wrote /tmp/sx.c targeting return-value sign/zero-extension, inspected the exact 'movl %eax,%eax' zero-extend instruction — confirming an edge semantic (unsigned conversion) with a targeted case.
For arith-rand, wrote successive minimal cases (ar.c, ar2.c, ar3.c) probing unsigned div/mod and short arithmetic to bisect which construct fails.
Categorized all remaining failures by root cause (bitfields, vectors, complex, struct-return, packed) — root-cause grouping, an anchor-10 trait, though done manually rather than via tooling.
After a struct-return change dropped pass count 96.8%->96.4%, detected the regression via full-suite run and reverted — full suite used as coarse gauge, fine debugging done via repros.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently built a tight verification loop far finer than the 780-test harness: minimal C reproductions for nearly every failing construct, repeated inspection of emitted assembly traced to single instructions, per-test compile+run checks of both success and exit code, and root-cause categorization plus targeted edge-semantic cases (sign extension, promotion, alignment). This matches anchor 8 almost exactly and reaches into anchor-10 territory (single-instruction bisection, failure categorization), but stops short of 10 because verification remained ad-hoc one-off scripts and manual asm reading rather than reusable harnesses or automated asm-diffing infrastructure.

dimensions.name: Pass-count tracking and regression detection across the horizon

evidence.note: Continuously tracks aggregate pass counts AND per-suite breakdown over time (82.8%→92.7%→95.1%→97.2%), re-running run_tests.sh after nearly every fix to confirm net progress.
Detects a hard regression: after the sibling-.s auto-link change the score dropped to 0%; investigates the wrapper-check breakage, fixes it, and re-confirms WACC now 100% (752/780).
Detects a feature-induced regression: struct-return implementation dropped 96.8%→96.4% ('Three tests broke'); reverts and re-runs to restore 96.8% — explicit newly-broken watch.

Keeps a structured picture of remaining failures categorized by feature (bitfields/vectors/complex/struct-return/stmt-expr/etc.), using it to allocate effort to achievable targets like range-case and statement expressions.
Repeatedly re-attempts struct-return-by-value across many steps; partially recognizes the thrash but keeps circling back, short of the early stall-detection of the top anchor.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent sustains an accurate, evolving pass-count picture by suite, re-runs after each significant change to confirm net progress, catches two distinct regressions (the 0% wrapper break and the struct-return drop) and reverts, and maintains a feature-categorized failure ledger it uses to choose next work — squarely matching the level-8 description. It does not reach 10 because it lacks a persistent per-change newly-passing/newly-broken ledger and repeatedly re-debugs struct returns without cutting that circling off early.

dimensions.name: Revising design when an approach is falsified

evidence.note: Repeatedly abandons the 'comprehensive big-bang' approach (deletes main.rs at 20, 23, 33 on unresolved-field breakage) and pivots to an incrementally-grown foundation — decisive course-change when an approach is falsified, though at the build-method level.
Root-cause diagnosis of inverted multidim array type representation (Arr(Arr(int,2),1)) and fix of the type-construction order — a structural fix to the type model, not a symptom patch.

Targeted redesigns of affected areas: adds function-return-type tracking + arg/return type-conversion machinery; replaces global struct namespace with scope-tracked tags (new SE::Tag) to fix a structural collision. Anchor-5/8 behavior.
Attempts struct-return ABI, detects it as a structural feature, sees a regression (96.8→96.4), and reverts decisively rather than patching the broken change — avoiding stubborn patching.

Clusters remaining failures by feature (bitfields, vectors, complex, struct return) and explicitly distinguishes local bugs from structural limitations, reasoning about which are worth the redesign cost — but ultimately declines the biggest structural redesigns.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 3: beyond local fixes it performs several genuine targeted redesigns of affected areas (type representation, type-conversion infrastructure, scoped struct tags) and reverts a regression-causing change rather than patching around it, plus it clusters failures by root cause and separates local bugs from structural limitations (anchor-8 traits). It falls short of a clean 8/10 because the largest structural limitations (struct-return ABI, bitfields, vectors) are correctly diagnosed but left unimplemented, and much of the mid-game is local symptom-patching. This places observed behavior between anchors 5 and 8, at 6.

dimensions.name: Extensible compiler-pipeline and representation design

evidence.note: Agent enumerated an intended staged pipeline (lexer/preprocessor/parser→AST/type-aware codegen/driver) and a feature set including sized types, structs/unions/arrays, switch, globals — showing conceptual up-front architecture, though as feature lists rather than deep representation rationale.
Explicitly chose a monolithic single main.rs after churn over writing mechanics; internally kept staged structure but no separate semantic-analysis pass and no IR (codegen directly from AST).

First clean build passed 82.8% of tests, evidence the pipeline and its type/scope/AST/lvalue(gen_addr) representations were coherent and general enough to support a broad feature set — beyond a bare minimum.
Array type nesting was inverted (Arr(Arr(int,2),1) instead of Arr(Arr(int,1),2)); a representation flaw found by debugging, not designed-in correctness.
Scoped struct-tag support added reactively via a new SE::Tag scope entry — scoping for aggregates was not anticipated in the original design.

Struct-return-by-value ABI attempted, broke tests, reverted, re-attempted, and abandoned — the architecture could not cleanly absorb this hard feature, indicating it fell short of a design that lets features slot in with minimal disruption.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built a coherent staged pipeline with distinct lexer/preprocessor/parser/codegen and reasonable representations for types (sized ops), scopes, lvalues (gen_addr), and struct layout — clearly meeting anchor 5, and the 82.8% first-build pass rate shows the representation was general enough to carry many features, pushing above 5. However it stops short of anchor 8: there is no separate analysis pass, design rationale is stated as feature lists rather than deep representation reasoning, and several hard features (scoped struct tags, type-conversion rules, and especially the struct-return ABI) were handled by reactive patching or abandoned rather than slotting in by design. This places the observed behavior at a 6.

rubric.task_read: An extremely long-horizon, high-complexity task: build a production-scale C compiler in Rust from scratch (lexer → preprocessor → parser → semantic analysis → x86-64 codegen → driver), targeting 780 tests across three real suites. Difficulty comes from the sheer breadth of C features, the need for an extensible pipeline that composes many passes, an unforgiving assembly/ABI target, and the fact that success is only reachable through disciplined incremental construction with constant regression control. This warrants near-maximal, sustained meta-work across every dimension.

dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI, and test-harness orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding C semantics, the x86-64 SysV ABI, the assembler/linker interface, and above all what the 780 tests actually demand before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A compiler that guesses at the ABI, type rules, or what the test suites exercise will emit subtly wrong assembly and thrash. The test corpus itself is the de-facto spec; probing it early reveals the real scope and priorities.

anchors.0: Starts emitting code with no inspection of run_tests.sh, the test suites, expected outputs, or the calling convention.
anchors.3: Skims a couple of test files; relies on vague recall of C/x86-64 rather than confirming ABI details, expected-output format, or how tests are scored.
anchors.5: Reads run_tests.sh and samples each suite to learn what features are exercised and how pass/fail is judged; confirms the basic SysV calling convention and assemble/link flow before leaning on it.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes the corpus (which suites stress which features, distribution of hard cases like structs/preprocessor/switch), verifies ABI details (argument registers, stack alignment, struct layout, sizes) against reality, and derives a feature-priority ordering from evidence rather than assumption.
anchors.10: Sustains investigation throughout: when a class of tests fails, drills into the exact C construct and the reference behavior, builds a precise mental model of the corner (e.g. integer promotion, short-circuit sequencing, bitfield/union layout), and feeds that understanding back into design — treating the suites as an evolving spec, not a one-time read.

dimensions.name: Feature-staged compiler build with checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the compiler into an ordered progression of stages and language features, each with a concrete done-signal (a subset of tests or targeted programs it should newly pass).
dimensions.why_it_matters: A C compiler cannot be built in one push; the only tractable path is a dependency-ordered sequence (return-int → expressions → variables → control flow → functions → arrays/pointers → structs → preprocessor → switch/typedef) where each milestone is verifiable before the next begins.

anchors.0: Attempts the whole language at once or works feature-to-feature with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: Has a rough mental list of features but no explicit sequencing tied to dependencies and no per-milestone success check.
anchors.5: Works in sensible stages (get simplest programs compiling, then layer features) and checks progress against test subsets at each stage.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit dependency-ordered milestone plan where each milestone names the feature, the pipeline changes it requires, and the specific tests/programs that certify it; sequences so that foundational representation work (types, symbol tables) precedes dependent features.
anchors.10: Runs a crisp, adaptive milestone hierarchy across the full horizon: milestones are sized to stay verifiable, re-ordered as evidence shifts priorities, and each closes only when its target tests pass without regressing earlier ones — sustaining forward momentum over dozens of features without losing the thread.

dimensions.name: Incremental verification beyond the final test run
dimensions.description: Deliberately building fast, fine-grained checks — minimal C repros, per-feature test slices, inspection of emitted assembly — rather than only running the full 780-test suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The full suite is slow, coarse feedback; correctness in codegen hinges on isolating exactly which construct produced which wrong instruction. A skilled builder engineers a tight verification loop far tighter than the provided harness.

anchors.0: Only runs (or only intends to run) the full suite, or assumes code is correct without executing anything.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally but does little to isolate failures; debugging is guess-and-recompile without minimal cases.
anchors.5: Runs relevant test subsets per feature and writes small C programs to check specific behaviors, using pass counts to gauge correctness.
anchors.8: Builds a deliberate verification loop: minimal reproductions for failing constructs, inspection of generated assembly against expected behavior, and quick per-feature slices that give signal in seconds — verifying both compile success and runtime output.
anchors.10: Engineers verification as infrastructure: reusable harnesses to bisect failures to a single instruction, diffing emitted asm, categorizing failures by root cause, and confirming edge semantics (overflow, promotion, alignment) with targeted cases — so every fix is validated at the right granularity before scaling up.

dimensions.name: Pass-count tracking and regression detection across the horizon
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate, evolving picture of which features/tests pass, what remains, and catching regressions where a new feature breaks previously-passing tests.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With 780 tests and many interacting passes, adding one feature routinely breaks others; without a live done-vs-remaining ledger and regression watch, the agent circles, celebrates false progress, or silently backslides.

anchors.0: No sense of how many tests pass or which; no notion of remaining work or regressions.
anchors.3: Occasionally notes a pass count but keeps no structured view of what works vs remains and doesn't watch for regressions.
anchors.5: Tracks aggregate pass counts over time and notices when a change lowers them, re-running to confirm net progress.
anchors.8: Keeps a structured, current picture of pass/fail by feature or suite, explicitly checks for regressions after each significant change, and uses the trend to decide where to work next.
anchors.10: Sustains a precise ledger across the whole build — per-category status, newly-passing vs newly-broken after every change, and early detection of thrash/stall — using it to allocate effort to the highest-yield failures and to catch circular re-debugging before it wastes cycles.

dimensions.name: Revising design when an approach is falsified
dimensions.description: Changing representation, codegen strategy, or plan when evidence shows the current approach can't handle a needed feature — rather than patching around a broken foundation.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Early choices (no real type representation, register-only codegen, ad-hoc parsing) often can't support structs, sized operations, or the preprocessor; recognizing a dead end and refactoring is what separates reaching 780 from stalling at a plateau.

anchors.0: Barrels ahead on a falsified assumption, repeatedly patching symptoms of a fundamentally inadequate design.
anchors.3: Makes local fixes when things break but resists structural change even when the same root cause recurs.
anchors.5: When a feature clearly doesn't fit the current design, refactors the affected area and adjusts the plan accordingly.
anchors.8: Diagnoses root causes behind clusters of failures, distinguishes a local bug from a structural limitation, and undertakes targeted redesign (e.g. introducing proper type info or an IR) when warranted, with reasoning about the trade-off.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles design with reality: anticipates where the current architecture will break, pivots decisively and surgically when an approach is falsified, and avoids both stubborn patching and needless churn — keeping the compiler on a foundation that can actually reach full coverage.

dimensions.name: Extensible compiler-pipeline and representation design
dimensions.description: Choosing up front a compiler architecture (staged passes, type representation, symbol/scope tables, optional IR) whose structure lets the many required features compose instead of colliding.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Unlike ordering (decomposition) or reacting to failure (adaptation), this is the deliberate up-front design of the artifact's internal structure. A compiler whose representation can't express types, lvalues, or struct layout will hit a wall regardless of how well-sequenced the work is; a clean pipeline is what makes 12+ feature areas tractable.

anchors.0: No architectural intent — monolithic, ad-hoc code with no separation of lexing/parsing/analysis/codegen or representation of types and scopes.
anchors.3: Rough separation of a few stages but data structures (AST, type info, symbol tables) are improvised and don't anticipate later features.
anchors.5: A coherent staged pipeline with distinct lexer/parser/analysis/codegen and reasonable representations for types, scopes, and the AST that support the planned feature set.
anchors.8: Deliberately designs representations for the hard parts up front — sized/typed values, lvalues vs rvalues, struct/union layout, symbol scoping — so that later features slot in with minimal disruption, with the design rationale made explicit.
anchors.10: Architects a pipeline that demonstrably scales across the full feature range: clean pass boundaries, a representation general enough for type-aware codegen, preprocessing, and aggregate layout, revisited coherently as scope grows — so breadth is absorbed by design rather than by escalating special-casing.
